title: Suno for OST + Opus for track and engine - does it sound too 'AI-y'?
author: Tasty-Ad-3753
selftext: I've been playing around with an F-Zero style game, and I'm quite happy with the tracks and flow of the play (excuse my bad driving). Do you think the OST sounds too obviously AI generated? Opus hasn't been amazing in terms of music quality so I'm just like embedding the MP3 directly in the tracks. Does anyone have a better workflow than this? any tips on how to generate good sound effects also appreciated as I don't know how to make those at all.

comments.author: Cold-Age7633
comments.body: Dont know answer to question, but want to know more about the game!

comments.author: Temporary-Ad2956
comments.body:
Game looks sick, can tell it was made by Suno (the music) but it’s not bad at all.

I tried a lot with Suno but never managed to get anything that didn’t sound Suno if you get me. Ended up connecting codex to Renoise and got it to lay down the tracks which got rid of that ai feel completely (but you do need to add your own music skills in to get it nice)

replies.author: Tasty-Ad-3753
replies.body: Ooh interesting - How close would you say the outputs were to what you wanted?

replies.author: Temporary-Ad2956
replies.body:
Hmmm if I keep it simple then quite close, definitely have to direct it more. It’s definitely not a one shot situation. I am making edm/techno music so this may not work for more complex genres.

But I found with Suno there wasn’t enough ways to direct it and tweak it, and splitting the audio into layers in Suno seemed to destroy the quality.

Another cool thing is you can script/extend Renoise easily with Astra/claude and integrate it into your workflow easily

comments.author: KrerdlyBeloved
comments.body:
A few things stand out to me, from experience:

\-The pixel font is very much AI-esque, and something that's carried over from Opus 5. I'd be able to pick it out pretty easily.

\-Similarly, the format of the text at the start: X - Y, is another give away, alongside the yellow bar on the left; that's pretty commonly seen with UI elements.
